newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields edge up as dust settles.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields edge up as dust settles.

text.p: *Australian bond yields edged higher in early trading as the dust settled after Friday's unexpected cut in official rates.
*Turnover was fairly light, partly due to the holiday in the U.S. for Memorial Day.
Australian bond yields edged higher in early trading as the dust settled after Friday's unexpected cut in official rates to 5.5 percent.

The weaker tone was largely in response to profit-taking by offshore investors during afterhours trading as they took advantage of the steep fall in yields as a result of the rate cut and a sharp tightening in yield differentials to the U.S.
"The market's digesting the stock that's come back from the offshore, but it's holding up pretty well. I suspect we are now going to see a couple of days of tight range trading," one trader said.
Overall turnover was fairly light, partly due to the holiday in the U.S. for Memorial Day.
U.S. Treasuries finished Friday's shortened session modestly higher in price before the long holiday weekend.

The local market faces a steady flow of data this week, including key components of the next week's first quarter GDP, but they are somewhat overshadowed with the rate cut in place. At this stage, the cut is seen as the last in the cycle.
Meanwhile, the U.S. faces a modest selection of data and Treasuries are more likely to be focused on the two- and five-year note sales on Wednesday and Thursday.

Long-dated spreads slightly underperforming against the dollar bloc after narrowing sharply on Friday after the rate cut. Canadian debt was little changed on Friday, while N.Z. bond yields were a touch high during a fairly illquid opening.
Local bond yield curve continues to steepen.
